Sure — **forget the big code** for a moment.  
Here’s the **simplest way to think + write `deleteAtEnd()`** in exam:

---

## 🧠 Logic (in plain words)

1️⃣ If list empty → nothing to delete  
2️⃣ If only one node → delete that node, head becomes NULL  
3️⃣ Otherwise →  
   - Move temp until **temp->next is last node**
   - Keep a **prev pointer** behind temp  
   - Link `prev->next = NULL`  
   - Free last node

---

## ✍️ Smallest clean code for `deleteAtEnd()`

```c
struct Node* deleteAtEnd(struct Node* head) {
    if (head == NULL)         // case 1: empty list
        return head;

    if (head->next == NULL) { // case 2: one node
        free(head);
        return NULL;
    }

    struct Node *temp = head, *prev = NULL;

    while (temp->next != NULL) { // case 3: many nodes
        prev = temp;
        temp = temp->next;
    }

    prev->next = NULL;
    free(temp);
    return head;
}
```

---

## 🧠 Ultra-short “Explanation” line (write in exam)

> "Traverse to the last node, keep track of previous node, update previous link to NULL, and free the last node."

---

### 🎯 Quick Cases for Viva

| List | Operation | Result |
|------|-----------|--------|
| EMPTY | delete end | stays empty |
| 10 | delete end | becomes empty |
| 10 → 20 → 30 | delete end | becomes 10 → 20 |

---

Got it. **You don’t want `prev` pointer**.  
Then the trick is simple:

👉 Stop **one node before the last**  
👉 That node will be the new last node  
👉 Free the node after it

---

## 🧠 Logic (No `prev` pointer)

- If list empty → nothing to delete
- If only one node → delete it → head = NULL
- Else:
  - Traverse until `temp->next->next == NULL`
    → Which means **temp is the second-last node**
  - Free `temp->next`
  - Make `temp->next = NULL`

---

## ▶️ EASIEST `deleteAtEnd()` Code — No `prev` Used

```c
struct Node* deleteAtEnd(struct Node* head) {
    if (head == NULL)         // empty list
        return head;

    if (head->next == NULL) { // only one node
        free(head);
        return NULL;
    }

    struct Node* temp = head;

    while (temp->next->next != NULL) { // stop at 2nd last node
        temp = temp->next;
    }

    free(temp->next); // delete last node
    temp->next = NULL;

    return head;
}
```

---

## ✍️ Tiny Theory Line for Exam

> "Traverse to the second-last node using `temp->next->next != NULL`, then free the last node and update `temp->next = NULL`."
